title: Isis and the Secret Name
subtitle: The goddess who tricked the sun himself into giving up his power

learningObjectives.text: How does Isis obtain Ra's secret name?
What does the name give her?

serpent.work: Legend of Ra and Isis, the serpent and Ra's illness
serpent.author: E. A. Wallis Budge
serpent.locator: Legend of Ra and Isis, the serpent and Ra's illness; local text normalized characters 37066-38149
serpent.excerpt: Soon after Isis had placed the serpent on the Path, Ra passed by, and the reptile bit him, thus injecting poison into his body. Its effect was terrible, and Ra cried out in agony. His jaws chattered, his lips trembled, and he became speechless for a time; never before had be suffered such pain. The gods hearing his cry rushed to him, and when he could speak he told them that he had been bitten by a deadly serpent. In spite of all the words of power which were known to him, and his secret name which had been hidden in his body at his birth, a serpent had bitten him, and he was being consumed with a fiery pain. He then commanded that all the gods who had any knowledge of magical spells should come to him, and when they came, Isis, the great lady of spells, the destroyer of diseases, and the revivifier of the dead, came with them. Turning to Ra she said, "What hath happened, O divine Father?" and in answer the god told her that a serpent had bitten him, that he was hotter than fire and colder than water, that his limbs quaked, and that he was losing the power of sight.

name.work: Legend of Ra and Isis, the hidden name
name.author: E. A. Wallis Budge
name.locator: Legend of Ra and Isis, the hidden name; local text normalized characters 38149-38706
name.excerpt: Then Isis said to him with guile, "Divine Father, tell me thy name, for he who uttereth his own name shall live." Thereupon Ra proceeded to enumerate the various things that he had done, and to describe his creative acts, and ended his speech to Isis by saying, that he was Khepera in the morning, Ra at noon, and Temu in the evening. Apparently he thought that the naming of these three great names would satisfy Isis, and that she would immediately pronounce a word of power and stop the pain in his body, which, during his speech, had become more acute.

transfer.work: Legend of Ra and Isis, transfer of the hidden name
transfer.author: E. A. Wallis Budge
transfer.locator: Legend of Ra and Isis, transfer of the hidden name; local text normalized characters 39033-39631
transfer.excerpt: Isis shall search in me, and my name shall pass from my body into hers." At that moment Ra removed himself from the sight of the gods in his Boat, and the Throne in the Boat of Millions of Years had no occupant. The great name of Ra was, it seems, hidden in his heart, and Isis, having some doubt as to whether Ra would keep his word or not, agreed with Horus that Ra must be made to take an oath to part with his two Eyes, that is, the Sun and the Moon. At length Ra allowed his heart to be taken from his body, and his great and secret name, whereby he lived, passed into the possession of Isis.

narrativeBlocks.title: A goddess who wants more
narrativeBlocks.body: Isis is already powerful — but the supreme power belongs to Ra, and it lives in his secret name. She resolves to take it, and her plan is worthy of a trickster.

narrativeBlocks.title: The serpent in the path
narrativeBlocks.body: She gathers Ra's own drool (in some versions, clay mixed with it) and shapes a serpent, laying it where the god walks each day. It bites him — and only she can cure the poison. The leverage is perfect.

narrativeBlocks.title: The price of the cure
narrativeBlocks.body: Ra suffers and calls for help; Isis offers her magic — but the cure works only if he speaks his secret name. The god who ruled by the power of his hidden name is forced to surrender it.

narrativeBlocks.title: The transfer
narrativeBlocks.body: He speaks it through her, and her power becomes equal to his — the myth's quiet thesis: names hold power, and knowing the true name of a thing (or god) is the deepest magic in Egypt.

narrativeBlocks.title: Isis the endless fixer
narrativeBlocks.body: This is the Isis pattern: she restores Osiris, raises Horus in hiding, and takes Ra's name — the goddess whose defining skill is making broken things whole and power hers when it matters.

quiz.prompt: How does Isis extract Ra's secret name?

choices.text: She steals it from his temple scroll
She wins it in a riddle contest
She makes a serpent of his own drool to bite him — then offers a cure that requires him to speak the name

quiz.explanation: The wound only she can heal is the leverage — the oldest 'poison-then-cure' trick.

quiz.prompt: What does the secret name represent?

choices.text: The supreme magical power — knowing the true name of a god means having his power

quiz.explanation: In Egyptian thought the hidden name IS the power — Isis doesn't borrow it, she takes it.
